fields.name: Users
fields.evidence: EoCClient.dll ecl::lariannet::TrackingSystem::ProcessBlockEvents clears this singleton (and the unblocked one) with EoCClient.dll+0x9C4D40: values first via +0x34C410 (IndexedStorage<ls::STDString>, stride 0x18, at +0x30), then keys (IndexedStorage<ls::Guid>, size at +0x2C). On a BlockedUser event (from TrackingSystem::OnUserBlocked(BlockedUser const&)) it inserts the Guid key and assigns the STDString from event+0x10 (user name). Live: all zero. Windows: the component destructor FUN_1406ca550 (registered by bg3.exe+0x66E220) runs FUN_1405da6d0 over the values at +0x30 - one 24-byte ls::STDString per key (stride 0x18, size/capacity at +0x10/+0x14, count = key count at +0x2C) - then frees them and destroys the key HashSet with the plain-key helper FUN_140582AD0: so the game build has 24-byte strings as values and trivially destructible keys (Guid in the Toolkit).

open_questions: The key width (16-byte Guid) comes from the Toolkit insert path; the Windows code read only shows trivially destructible keys.
second_pass: Value stride and type confirmed on Windows (destructor FUN_1406ca550 -> FUN_1405da6d0: 24-byte STDString per entry at +0x30; key set destroyed as plain keys), so the Toolkit-derived HashMap<Guid, STDString> holds for bg3.exe.
live_reason: only empty (all-zero) instances were seen: the member boundaries are untested
